talents.name: Channel Aggression
talents.benefit: If you succeed on an attack against a flanked opponent or any target that is denied its Dexterity bonus to Reflex Defense, you may spend a Force Point as a free action to deal additional damage to the target equal to 1d6 per class level (maximum 10d6).
talents.summary: After hitting a flanked or Dexterity-denied target, spend a Force Point as a free action for +1d6 damage per class level, max 10d6.

talents.name: Channel Anger
talents.benefit: You let your anger swell into a rage. As a swift action, you may spend a Force Point to gain a +2 rage bonus on melee attack rolls and melee damage rolls for a number of rounds equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier. At the end of this duration, you move -1 step along the condition track (see Conditions, page 148). While raging, you cannot use skills that require patience and concentration, such as Mechanics, Stealth, or Use the Force.
talents.summary: Spend a Force Point to rage for 5 + Con modifier rounds, gaining +2 melee attack and damage, then move 1 step down the condition track.

talents.name: Crippling Strike
talents.benefit: Whenever you score a critical hit, you may spend a Force Point to also reduce the target's speed by half until he is fully healed (that is, restored to maximum hit points).
talents.summary: On a critical hit, spend a Force Point to halve the target's speed until it is restored to full hit points.

talents.name: Embrace the Dark Side
talents.benefit: Whenever you use a Force power with the [dark side] descriptor, you may reroll your Use the Force check, but you must accept the result of the reroll even if it is worse. Upon choosing this talent, you can no longer use Force powers with the [light side] descriptor.
talents.summary: Reroll Use the Force checks for dark-side powers and keep the reroll, but permanently lose access to light-side Force powers.

talents.name: Force Power Adept
talents.benefit: You are skilled at using a particular Force power. Select one Force power you know. When using that Force power, you have the option of spending a Force Point to make two Use the Force checks, keeping the better result.
talents.special: This talent may be selected multiple times. Its effects do not stack. Each time you select this talent, you must choose a different Force power.
talents.summary: Choose a Force power; when using it, spend a Force Point to roll Use the Force twice and keep the better result.

talents.name: Force Treatment
talents.benefit: You can make a Use the Force check in place of a Treat Injury check (see the Treat Injury skill, page 74). You are considered trained in the Treat Injury skill for purposes of using this talent. If you are entitled to a Treat Injury check reroll, you may reroll your Use the Force check instead (subject to the same circumstances and limitations). In addition, you can administer first aid, treat disease, treat poison, and treat radiation without the requisite medical kit or medpac.
talents.summary: Use Use the Force for Treat Injury, count as trained, and perform several treatments without a medical kit or medpac.

talents.name: Fortified Body
talents.benefit: The Force shields you against ailments, toxins, and radiation poisoning, making you immune to disease, poison, and radiation.
talents.summary: You are immune to disease, poison, and radiation.

talents.name: Attune Weapon
talents.benefit: You may spend a Force Point to attune a melee weapon. Attuning the weapon takes a full-round action. From that point forward, whenever you wield the attuned weapon, you gain a +1 Force bonus on attack rolls. The weapon is attuned to you alone; others who wield the weapon do not gain the Force bonus.
talents.summary: Spend a Force Point and a full-round action to attune a melee weapon, granting you +1 Force bonus on attacks with it.

talents.name: Empower Weapon
talents.benefit: You may spend a Force Point to empower a melee weapon. Empowering the weapon takes a full-round action. From that point forward, the empowered weapon deals an additional die of damage, but only when wielded by you. (For example, an empowered lightsaber deals 3d8 points of damage instead of 2d8 points of damage.) Others who wield the weapon do not gain the bonus damage die.
talents.summary: Spend a Force Point and full-round action to empower a melee weapon so it deals one extra damage die when you wield it.

talents.name: Force Talisman
talents.benefit: You may spend one Force Point to imbue a weapon or some other portable object with the Force, creating a talisman that provides protection to you. Creating the talisman takes a full-round action. While you wear or carry the talisman on your person, you gain a +1 Force bonus to one of your defenses (Reflex, Fortitude, or Will). You may only have one Force talisman active at any given time, and if your Force talisman is destroyed, you may not create another Force talisman for 24 hours.
talents.summary: Spend a Force Point and full-round action to create a talisman granting +1 Force bonus to one chosen defense while you carry it.

talents.name: Greater Force Talisman
talents.benefit: As Force Talisman (above), except that the talisman's Force bonus extends to all three of your defenses (Reflex, Fortitude, and Will).
talents.summary: Your Force Talisman's +1 Force bonus applies to Reflex, Fortitude, and Will instead of only one defense.

talents.name: Debilitating Shot
talents.benefit: If you aim before making a ranged attack (see Aim, page 154) and the attack hits, you move the target -1 step along the condition track (see Conditions, page 148) in addition to dealing damage.
talents.summary: If you aim before a ranged attack and hit, move the target 1 step down the condition track in addition to dealing damage.

talents.name: Deceptive Shot
talents.benefit: Select one target in line of sight within 6 squares. You can spend two swift actions on the same turn to make a Deception check; if the check result equals or exceeds the target's Will Defense, the target is denied its Dexterity bonus to Reflex Defense against your attacks until the beginning of your next turn.
talents.summary: Spend two swift actions to beat a nearby target's Will Defense with Deception, denying its Dexterity bonus to Reflex Defense against your attacks.

talents.name: Improved Quick Draw
talents.benefit: If you are carrying a pistol (either in your hand or in a holster), you may draw the pistol and make a single attack during a surprise round even if you are surprised. If you are not surprised, you may take any single action of your choice, as normal.
talents.summary: Even when surprised, draw a carried pistol and make one attack during the surprise round.

talents.name: Knockdown Shot
talents.benefit: If you aim before making a ranged attack (see Aim, page 154) and the attack hits, you knock the target prone in addition to dealing damage. You can't use this talent to knock down targets two or more size categories bigger than you.
talents.summary: If you aim before a ranged attack and hit, also knock the target prone unless it is at least two size categories larger than you.

talents.name: Multiattack Proficiency (pistols)
talents.benefit: Whenever you make multiple attacks with any type of pistol as a full attack action (see Full Attack, page 154), you reduce the penalty on your attack rolls by 2.
talents.special: You can take this talent multiple times; each time you take this talent, you reduce the penalty on your attack rolls by an additional 2.
talents.summary: Reduce the full-attack penalty with pistols by 2; repeated selections reduce it by another 2 each.

talents.name: Force Fortification
talents.benefit: As a reaction, you can spend a Force Point to negate a critical hit scored against you and take normal damage instead. You can spend this Force Point even if you've already spent a Force Point earlier in the round.
talents.summary: As a reaction, spend a Force Point to turn a critical hit against you into a normal hit, even if you already spent a Force Point this round.

talents.name: Greater Weapon Focus (Lightsabers)
talents.benefit: You gain a +1 bonus on melee attack rolls with lightsabers. This bonus stacks with the bonus granted by the Weapon Focus (lightsabers) feat.
talents.summary: Gain +1 on melee attacks with lightsabers, stacking with Weapon Focus.

talents.name: Greater Weapon Specialization (Lightsabers)
talents.benefit: You gain a +2 bonus on melee damage rolls with lightsabers. This bonus stacks with the bonus granted by the Weapon Specialization (lightsabers) talent.
talents.prerequisites: Greater Weapon Focus (lightsabers), Weapon Focus (lightsabers), Weapon Specialization (lightsabers)
talents.summary: Gain +2 melee damage with lightsabers, stacking with Weapon Specialization.

talents.name: Multiattack Proficiency (lightsabers)
talents.benefit: Whenever you make multiple attacks with any type of lightsaber as a full attack action (see Full Attack, page 154), you reduce the penalty on your attack rolls by 2.
talents.special: You can take this talent multiple times; each time you take this talent, you reduce the penalty on your attack rolls by an additional 2.
talents.summary: Reduce the full-attack penalty with lightsabers by 2; repeated selections reduce it by another 2 each.

talents.name: Severing Strike
talents.benefit: When you deal damage with a lightsaber that is equal to or greater than both the target's current hit points and the target's damage threshold (that is, when you would deal enough damage to kill your target), you may choose to use this talent. Instead of dealing full damage, you instead deal half damage to your target and move it -1 step on the condition track (see Conditions, page 148). In addition, you sever one of your target's arms at the wrist or elbow joint, or one of the target's legs at the knee or ankle joint (your choice). Severing part of an arm prevents the target from wielding weapons or using tools in that hand and imposes a -5 penalty on skill checks and ability checks keyed to Strength and Dexterity. Severing part of a leg knocks the target prone, reduces the target's speed by half, reduces its carrying capacity by half, and imposes a -5 penalty on skill checks and ability checks keyed to Strength and Dexterity. Because of the severity of such an injury, losing a part of a limb causes a persistent condition that can only be removed by having surgery successfully performed on you (see Treat Injury skill, page 74). A cybernetic replacement limb (see page 137) negates these reductions and penalties.
talents.summary: Instead of killing a target with a threshold-beating lightsaber hit, deal half damage, move it 1 step down the track, and sever an arm or leg with lasting penalties.

talents.name: Ataru
talents.benefit: You may add your Dexterity bonus (instead of your Strength bonus) on damage rolls when wielding a lightsaber. When you wield a lightsaber two-handed, you may apply double your Dexterity bonus (instead of double your Strength bonus) to the damage.
talents.summary: Use Dexterity instead of Strength for lightsaber damage, doubling Dexterity when wielding the lightsaber two-handed.

talents.name: Djem So
talents.benefit: Once per round when an opponent hits you with a melee attack, you may spend a Force Point as a reaction to make an immediate attack against that opponent.
talents.summary: Once per round when hit by a melee attack, spend a Force Point as a reaction to attack that opponent immediately.

talents.name: Jar'Kai
talents.benefit: When you use the Lightsaber Defense talent, you gain twice the normal deflection bonus to your Reflex Defense when you are wielding two lightsabers.
talents.summary: While wielding two lightsabers, double the Reflex Defense bonus from Lightsaber Defense.

talents.name: Juyo
talents.benefit: Once per encounter, you may spend a Force Point as a swift action to designate a single enemy in your line of sight. For the remainder of the encounter, you may reroll your first attack roll each round against that opponent, keeping the better result.
talents.prerequisites: Weapon Focus (lightsabers), Weapon Specialization (lightsabers), base attack bonus +10
talents.summary: Once per encounter, spend a Force Point to designate a visible enemy and reroll your first attack against it each round, keeping the better roll.

talents.name: Makashi
talents.benefit: When wielding a single lightsaber in one hand, the deflection bonus you gain from the Lightsaber Defense talent (see page 41) increases by 2 (to a maximum of +5).
talents.summary: With one one-handed lightsaber, increase your Lightsaber Defense deflection bonus by 2, up to +5.

talents.name: Niman
talents.benefit: When wielding a lightsaber, you gain a +1 bonus to your Reflex Defense and Will Defense.
talents.summary: While wielding a lightsaber, gain +1 Reflex Defense and +1 Will Defense.

talents.name: Shien
talents.benefit: Whenever you redirect a deflected blaster bolt (see the Redirect Shot talent, page 41), you gain a +5 bonus on your ranged attack roll.
talents.summary: Gain +5 on the ranged attack roll when using Redirect Shot.

talents.name: Shii-Cho
talents.benefit: When using the Block or Deflect talents, you only take a -2 penalty on your Use the Force check for every previous block or deflect attempt since your last turn (see page 41).
talents.summary: Reduce the cumulative Block/Deflect Use the Force penalty from -5 to -2 per previous attempt since your last turn.

talents.name: Sokan
talents.benefit: You may take 10 on Acrobatics checks to tumble even when distracted or threatened. Additionally, each threatened or occupied square that you tumble through only counts as 1 square of movement.
talents.summary: Take 10 when tumbling under pressure, and threatened or occupied squares cost only 1 square of movement while tumbling.

talents.name: Soresu
talents.benefit: You may reroll a failed Use the Force check when using the Block or Deflect talents.
talents.summary: Reroll a failed Use the Force check made for Block or Deflect.

talents.name: Trakata
talents.benefit: By harnessing the unique characteristics of a lightsaber, you can catch your opponent off guard by quickly shutting off and reigniting the blade. When wielding a lightsaber, you may spend two swift actions to make a Deception check to feint in combat (see page 66).
talents.prerequisites: Weapon Focus (lightsabers), Weapon Specialization (lightsabers), base attack bonus +12
talents.summary: While wielding a lightsaber, spend two swift actions to make a Deception check to feint in combat.

talents.name: Vaapad
talents.benefit: When attacking with a lightsaber, you score a critical hit on a natural roll of 19 or 20. However, a natural 19 is not considered an automatic hit; if you roll a natural 19 and still miss the target, you do not score a critical hit.
talents.prerequisites: Juyo, Weapon Focus (lightsabers), Weapon Specialization (lightsabers), base attack bonus +12
talents.summary: Lightsaber attacks score critical hits on natural 19-20, though a natural 19 still has to hit normally.

talents.name: Assault Tactics
talents.benefit: As a move action, you may designate a single creature or object as the target of an assault. If you succeed on a DC 15 Knowledge (tactics) check, you and all allies able to hear and understand you deal +1d6 points of damage to the target with each successful melee or ranged attack, until the start of your next turn. This is a mind-affecting effect.
talents.summary: As a move action, pass DC 15 Knowledge (tactics) to let you and hearing allies deal +1d6 damage to one target until your next turn.

talents.name: Deployment Tactics
talents.benefit: You can use your tactical knowledge to direct allies in battle. As a move action, you can make a DC 15 Knowledge (tactics) check. If the check succeeds, you and any allies that can see, hear, and understand you gain a +1 competence bonus on attack rolls against flanked opponents or a +1 dodge bonus to Reflex Defense against attacks of opportunity (your choice). The bonus lasts until the start of your next turn. This is a mind-affecting effect. If you have the Born Leader talent (page 44) or the Battle Analysis talent (page 52), the bonus granted by this talent increases to +2.
talents.summary: Pass DC 15 Knowledge (tactics) to grant you and aware allies +1 against flanked foes or +1 Reflex vs opportunity attacks until your next turn; certain talents raise it to +2.

talents.name: Field Tactics
talents.benefit: You know how to use existing terrain to best advantage. By using a move action, you can make a DC 15 Knowledge (tactics) check. If the check succeeds, you and all allies within 10 squares of you can use whatever cover is available to gain a +10 cover bonus to Reflex Defense (instead of the normal +5 cover bonus). Allies must be able to hear and understand you to gain this benefit, and the bonus lasts until the start of your next turn. This talent provides no benefit to anyone who doesn't have cover. This is a mind-affecting effect.
talents.summary: Pass DC 15 Knowledge (tactics) to improve available cover to +10 Reflex for you and nearby hearing allies until your next turn.

talents.name: One for the Team
talents.benefit: As a reaction, you can choose to take one-half or all of the damage dealt to an adjacent ally by a single attack. Similarly, as a reaction, an adjacent ally can choose to take one-half or all of the damage dealt to you by a single attack (even if he doesn't have this talent).
talents.summary: As a reaction, you and an adjacent ally can shift half or all damage from a single attack between each other.

talents.name: Outmaneuver
talents.benefit: An officer learns to counter the tactics of his enemies. As a standard action, you can make a DC 15 Knowledge (tactics) check. If the check succeeds, enemies in your line of sight lose all competence, insight, and morale bonuses on attack rolls, as well as any dodge bonuses to Reflex Defense, until the start of your next turn. If one or more enemy officers are within your line of sight, the highest-level officer among them can attempt to oppose your Knowledge (tactics) check as a reaction. If her skill check result is higher than yours, your attempt to outmaneuver your enemies fails.
talents.summary: Pass DC 15 Knowledge (tactics) to strip visible enemies of specified attack and Reflex bonuses until your next turn; an enemy officer can oppose the check.

talents.name: Shift Defense I
talents.benefit: As a swift action, you can take a -2 penalty to one defense (Reflex, Fortitude, or Will) to gain a +1 competence bonus to another defense until the start of your next turn.
talents.summary: As a swift action, take -2 to one defense to gain +1 competence to another until your next turn.

talents.name: Shift Defense II
talents.benefit: As a swift action, you can take a -5 penalty to one defense (Reflex, Fortitude, or Will) to gain a +2 competence bonus to another defense until the start of your next turn.
talents.summary: As a swift action, take -5 to one defense to gain +2 competence to another until your next turn.

talents.name: Shift Defense III
talents.benefit: As a swift action, you can gain a +5 competence bonus to one defense (Reflex, Fortitude, or Will) by taking a -5 penalty to your other two defenses.
talents.prerequisites: Shift Defense I, Shift Defense II
talents.summary: As a swift action, gain +5 competence to one defense by taking -5 to the other two.

talents.name: Tactical Edge
talents.benefit: You can use the Assault Tactics, Deployment Tactics, or Field Tactics talent as a swift action instead of a move action, provided you have the talent in question.
talents.summary: Use Assault Tactics, Deployment Tactics, or Field Tactics as a swift action instead of a move action.

talents.name: Dark Healing
talents.benefit: You can spend a Force Point to heal wounds by drawing life energy from another creature within 6 squares of you. Using this ability is a standard action, and you must succeed on a ranged attack roll. If the attack equals or exceeds the target's Fortitude Defense, you deal 1d6 points of damage per class level to the target and you heal an equal amount. If the attack fails, there is no effect.
talents.summary: Spend a Force Point and a standard action to make a ranged attack vs Fortitude; on success deal 1d6 damage per class level and heal the same amount.

talents.name: Dark Scourge
talents.benefit: You have dedicated your life to wiping out the Jedi, and your hatred of them knows no bounds. Against Jedi characters, you gain a +1 dark side bonus on attack rolls.
talents.summary: Gain +1 dark side bonus on attack rolls against Jedi characters.

talents.name: Dark Side Adept
talents.benefit: Force powers that are strongly tied to the dark side flow through you more easily. You can reroll any Use the Force check made when activating Force powers with the [dark side] descriptor, but you must keep the result of the reroll, even if it is worse.
talents.summary: Reroll Use the Force checks for dark-side Force powers, but keep the reroll.

talents.name: Dark Side Master
talents.benefit: As Dark Side Adept (see above), except that you can spend a Force Point and keep the better of the two Use the Force checks.
talents.summary: When using Dark Side Adept, spend a Force Point to keep the better of the two Use the Force checks.

talents.name: Force Deception
talents.benefit: You can use your Use the Force check modifier instead of your Deception check modifier when making Deception checks, as you use the Force to cloak your vile treachery. You are considered trained in the Deception skill for purposes of using this talent. If you are entitled to a Deception check reroll, you may reroll your Use the Force check instead (subject to the same circumstances and limitations).
talents.summary: Use your Use the Force modifier for Deception checks, count as trained in Deception, and apply eligible Deception rerolls to the substituted check.

talents.name: Improved Dark Healing
talents.benefit: Your dark healing ability (see above) improves. The range of this ability increases to 12 squares, and even if the attack fails the target takes half damage while you heal an equal amount.
talents.summary: Dark Healing reaches 12 squares; on a failed attack the target still takes half damage and you heal the same amount.

talents.name: Wicked Strike
talents.benefit: When you score a critical hit with a lightsaber, you may spend a Force Point to move the target -2 steps along the condition track (see Conditions, page 148).
talents.summary: On a lightsaber critical hit, spend a Force Point to move the target 2 steps down the condition track.
